clue.text: Obsolete language Switzerland will replace in the morning

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so one piece is swapped out of the language for another

parts.note: the ancient Semitic language spoken in biblical times
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A dead tongue is pushed out of morning lessons in favour of Swiss studies.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, from Confoederatio Helvetica, appears on Swiss car stickers and web addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic is so old-fashioned that it has fallen out of use, which is what obsolete describes.

clue.text: Notice seal is devoted

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice
an O-ring is a rubber loop used as a seal in machinery

explanation.surface: A notice says a seal is loyal, like a faithful pet.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoring fan is utterly loving and loyal, so they are devoted to the one they admire.

clue.text: Conservative Society is extremely treacherous, and is free from contradiction

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative in British politics
S is the abbreviation for society
taken as written

indicators.note: at the extremes means only the first and last letters of the following word

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Tory club proves thoroughly disloyal yet claims to be perfectly coherent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are Britain's main right-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense, to consist with something is to agree or be compatible with it, so to be without contradiction.

clue.text: Starting late, work-shy midwife on vacation makes unleavened bread

indicators.note: beginning late means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lazy means unwilling to work

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside letters go and only the outer two stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An idle midwife clocks in late and goes on holiday, leaving bread unrisen.
explanation.definitionFit: Azyme is an old word for the flat bread without yeast eaten at Passover, called matzo.

clue.text: Sometimes they navigate watercourses, following fish

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the watercourses are placed behind the fish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
rivers are natural watercourses

explanation.surface: Fish follow river routes when they navigate.
explanation.walkthrough: Rally co-drivers read pace notes to the driver, which is why the definition hedges with 'Sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rally driving the co-driver sits beside the driver reading the route notes, so co-drivers often navigate.

clue.text: Wild, if beer hall has odd characters ejected

indicators.note: throwing out the first, third, fifth letters and so on keeps only the even-placed ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A rowdy drinking hall throws out its strange customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' sounds like eccentric drinkers being bounced, but it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral animal has gone back to living untamed in nature after domestication, so it is wild.

clue.text: Uplifting tablet provided boost

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine
if means on condition that, provided

explanation.surface: A cheering pill gives someone a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: PILL and IF are joined, and the whole string is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or something that perks things up, which is a boost.

clue.text: I put in schedule: Make merry

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so the letter sits within the list

parts.note: a roster is a schedule of duties
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone books time in the diary for partying.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously, an old word for making merry.

clue.text: Reason American soldier enters places briefly

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the soldier goes into the other word
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: loci is the Latin plural of locus, a place
GI is the nickname for a US soldier

explanation.surface: The reason a US soldier briefly enters certain locations.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCI is the Latin plural of locus, common in maths and crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the faculty of sound thinking and argument, which reason also names.

clue.text: The moment music producer with shaved head was missing wife

indicators.note: a shaved head has lost its top, so the first letter is removed
missing means lacking, so the abbreviation for wife is taken away

parts.note: a bassoon is a woodwind instrument, something that produces music
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A record producer with a shaven head misses his wife the moment she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music producer' looks like a person in a studio; it is an instrument. BASSOON loses B, and WAS loses W.
explanation.definitionFit: As soon as means immediately when, the instant something happens, which is what the moment means in a sentence.

clue.text: My parts extremely shrunken, leading to derision

indicators.note: the outer letters are parted to make room for the exclamation in between
at the extremes means only the first and last letters of the following word are used

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!

explanation.surface: Someone's private parts have shrunk, and the result is mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation here, not a possessive, and 'parts' is a verb splitting the outer letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn is open contempt, and derision is the mocking expression of that same contempt.

clue.text: Singing and shouting, taking too many drugs

indicators.note: the shouting word takes in, or swallows, the drugs abbreviation inside itself

parts.note: yelling is shouting loudly
OD stands for overdose

explanation.surface: A wild partygoer is singing and shouting after overdoing the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is a style of singing that flips rapidly between chest voice and falsetto, typical of Alpine song.

clue.text: First female in workplace becoming rather impatient, at first, for opening

indicators.note: one thing turning into another means a letter is swapped for new ones

parts.note: an office is a place of work
F is the standard abbreviation for female; 'First' picks the first of the two in the word

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of each of the preceding two words is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The first woman in the office quickly grows impatient waiting for a vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first of the two Fs in OFFICE is replaced by RI.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or vent in the body or a structure, the same thing as an opening.

clue.text: I would twitch around ten, which is ludicrous

indicators.note: the first pair of words is placed around the number, enclosing it in the middle

parts.note: I'd, the contraction, without its apostrophe
10 written with letters that look like the digits
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A speaker admits they'd get a nervous twitch at ten o'clock, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten is written as the digits 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idiotic is so foolish that it seems laughable, which is what ludicrous means.

clue.text: Racist dithering about Republican

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned about and placed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A bigot is vacillating over a Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Night riders were mounted, masked white supremacists in the American South, such as the Ku Klux Klan, who terrorised Black people after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A night rider was a member of a violent white supremacist gang, so the noun names a racist by example.

clue.text: Page that's blank after line abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A page is left empty once a line of text has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' seems to mean the line is deleted, but it signals the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An interleaf is an extra sheet, usually unprinted, bound between the ordinary pages of a book.

clue.text: Summons dwarf regularly to get sex

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at fixed intervals, here every other one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A dwarf is called up routinely for intercourse, a deliberately silly scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, and a summons ordering someone to appear is one kind.

clue.text: I see boring Renaissance artist from Pacific island

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Titian was a great Venetian painter of the Renaissance
Ah! is said when something is understood, like I see

explanation.surface: A viewer finds an old master's painting dull, coming from a South Seas island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling into the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahitian is the adjective for people or things from Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Experts there making fizzy wine

parts.note: pros are professionals or experts
ecco is Italian for there it is

explanation.surface: Experienced hands there are producing sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: ECCO is the Italian for 'there!' or 'behold', apt for an Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosecco is a sparkling white wine from north-east Italy, so it is a fizzy wine.

clue.text: He maybe recalled a long story

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: He is the symbol for helium, an example of a gas
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man perhaps remembered a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun for the storyteller, but it is the chemical symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is an extended narrative, originally a medieval Norse tale of heroes, so a long story.

clue.text: Astronomer in Jesus' home losing footing, getting old

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry is its bottom, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Jesus grew up in Nazareth in the region of Galilee
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A stargazer slips while visiting the Holy Land in later life.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who used the telescope to study the moons of Jupiter.

clue.text: He attracts eccentric with difficulty

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man struggles to win over an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a stretch means only just managing it with great effort, so only barely and with difficulty.

clue.text: Architect ran site showing passage

indicators.note: showing means putting on display, so the letters are visible inside the words

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, then the next word, then the start of the third

explanation.surface: An architect managed a building site with a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Architect' looks like an anagram cue for 'ran site', but the letters do not fit; they sit inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across a place, so it is passage.

clue.text: Early people-carrier (Australian pick-up truck) with corrosion reduced

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ute, short for utility vehicle, is the Australian word for a pick-up
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: An old minibus, beside a rusty Australian truck, sounds like a car-dealer's listing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People-carrier' sounds like a minivan, but here it means a carrier of people before they are born.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb carries a baby through pregnancy, so it is the place that carries a person at the earliest stage of life.

clue.text: Model lost her case

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model has mislaid her suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the person who lost the case, but it is a verb telling you to reshape the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather pouch for carrying a pistol, a kind of case.

clue.text: Leave brothel!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for go away, clear off

definitions.note: read jokily as two slang words, ho (prostitute) and pit (den)
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split as two slang words, a prostitute's den

explanation.walkthrough: Hop it is British slang for go away; split the other way it is HO PIT, a cheeky picture of a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an imperative telling someone to leave at once, and read as two nouns it names a den of prostitutes.

clue.text: Fall about instead of beginning to embrace counterpoint

indicators.note: instead of means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a descent is a fall or drop
a. is an abbreviation for about, as in dates

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Collapse rather than starting a hug, set against something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of DESCENT gives way to A. 'Fall about' suggests laughing helplessly, but the words are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung above the main tune, a form of counterpoint in music.

clue.text: Woman is supporting upwardly mobile staff

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting beneath, so this piece comes last
moving upwards in a down clue means reading the letters from the bottom

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman props up her ambitious employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly mobile staff' suggests ambitious employees, but staff is a stick here.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris is a female first name, and crosswords often define a name by a general word for its bearer.

clue.text: Make a couple of deliveries to Spooner for native of the far north

indicators.note: Spooner was the clergyman famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: in cricket, to send down two balls is to bowl a pair; swap the opening sounds B and P

explanation.surface: A courier makes two drops to a reverend gentleman in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowl a pair becomes pole a bear when the first sounds swap. In cricket a delivery is one ball sent down by the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear lives only on Arctic sea ice, so it is a native animal of the far north.

clue.text: Rib functions lessened

indicators.note: lessened means reduced, so the last of these letters is dropped

parts.note: cos and tan, short for cosine and tangent, are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: Bodily functions are reduced around the ribcage.
explanation.walkthrough: Two trigonometric functions, COS and TAN, are joined and TAN loses its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the Latin anatomical term for a rib, used in medicine and in crosswords.

clue.text: American sweetheart blows horn, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a US term of endearment for a woman or girl
second meaning: sounds a horn or similar with short blasts

explanation.surface: An American girlfriend honks a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is US slang for darling or babe, while the verb means sounding a short horn blast.

clue.text: Produce cry at Silverstone?

parts.note: Silverstone is the British motor-racing circuit that hosts Formula 1; F1 is read as FI
to shout is to cry out

explanation.surface: A shout goes up at Silverstone, the British Formula 1 track.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that F1 is being treated as the letters FI.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish something out is to pull it from a pocket or bag and bring it forth, which is producing it.
